stories.title: The Knicks have a bench guard conundrum
stories.summary: Mike Brown is struggling to find the minutes for the team’s plentiful guard depth.
stories.detailText: NEW YORK, NY - DECEMBER 1: Tyler Kolek #13 and Miles McBride #2 of the New York Knicks high five during the game against the New Orleans Pelicans on December 1, 2024 at Madison Square Garden in New York City, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2024 NBAE (Photo by Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images When you’re the defending champions, there are not many holistic things to complain about. Sure, the Knicks started 0-3 with a very unsettling offense, but all they needed was their medicine (the Nets and Bulls) to get back to .500? Worried about losing to Philadelphia twice in October? Joel Embiid’s plantar fasciitis has already acted up; calm down. Any “problems” this early in the season are either short-term, regarding the looming extension talks, or good problems, which are more conundrums than actual problems. The biggest of those conundrums has to do with the Knicks’ rotation, specifically with their copious amounts of guard depth. Jalen Brunson is the head of the snake, but after him? There are a lot of players with minutes who could fluctuate on any given night. Tyler Kolek and Jose Alvarado duel over backup ball-handler minutes. Jordan Clarkson and Deuce McBride grapple over bench two-guard minutes. Landry Shamet’s strong play is actively pushing starters Mikal Bridges and Josh Hart over their minutes with the three entrenched parts of the team’s nucleus. It does qualify as a good problem to have, as injuries will undoubtedly give each of these guys ample opportunity over the course of 82 games, but when they’re all healthy, like they are right now? It probably gives Mike Brown a bigger headache than watching Andre Drummond attempt layups. All of these guys provide something that the Knicks could use more of, but have warts that can limit their playing time. Kolek is the best true playmaker, but he’s a poor defender, and his jump shot has been consistent throughout his young NBA career. This basically also describes Alvarado, but the defense is better from the New York native. McBride has stretches where he’s the team’s best rate shooter and is a tremendously pesky point-of-attack defender… but is that not what the team is getting out of a taller two-guard in Shamet? Clarkson has been a sparkplug every game he’s played this year, but the 35-year-old showed his maddening inconsistency in his first year in New York. It’s created an extremely volatile rotation, which isn’t surprising when you have a coach who opened the year saying only five players on this team have minutes that are secured. Mike Brown took the Knicks' starting five aside, looked at his bench players today at practice and said: "Everybody else in this gym, you're fighting – either to make the team or for minutes" pic.twitter.com/GweTAITsOT — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 7, 2026 Despite zero Knicks players averaging more than 33 minutes a game except Brunson (who’s at 34.1), only Shamet is averaging more than 18 minutes a game off the bench. McBride is at 17.5, Kolek is at 12.2, Alvarado is at 11.3, and Clarkson is at 9.9, but even these are deceiving. Kolek has played steady rotation minutes, but didn’t play at all in the first two games before Alvarado’s ankle injury. Alvarado played 16 and 11 minutes, got hurt, got benched after nine minutes on Monday, and was on track to be a DNP-CD against the Bulls on Wednesday. Clarkson’s gone from playing three, five, or eight minutes to his spurts of 15 and 17 in the two games against the Bulls and his 11 to spark the incredible fourth quarter against Brooklyn. McBride, who’s served as the Knicks’ sixth man for over two years now, has topped 17 minutes just twice. He played a season-low 11 minutes on Wednesday and hasn’t had a clear role. To get these guys more minutes, it would mean cutting minutes from Hart or Bridges. While both have their warts, and the latter continues to look somehow less involved than he was during his lowest moments last season, some of the Knicks’ best lineups are coming with them on the court… just separated. The Knicks most used lineups this season: pic.twitter.com/lVxDcEBps7 — Knicks Nation (@KnicksNation) November 5, 2026 We’ve seen Brown deploy line changes significantly more in the early going, opting to sub in three or four players at a time to deploy uniform units, but that’s not helping how erratic this all feels. The depth is making players redundant on the court, especially with how unwise it is to run four-guard lineups in an NBA that’s prioritizing size and length more and more. And with the Knicks’ extremely shallow forward and center depth? This glut might have to be sorted out at the trade deadline. As much as McBride has shown his tremendous value to the Knicks over the course of his contract, if he isn’t going to play more, is it even a net positive to keep him for the playoff run? For now, it’s merely a conundrum that Coach Brown will be scratching his head over every game. By the time we hit February? Things better be sorting themselves out.

stories.title: Yahoo Perfect 5: Luka Dončić, Evan Mobley and Walker Kessler lead my Friday lineup
stories.summary: Fantasy basketball analyst Dan Titus shares his lineup for Yahoo Perfect 5.
stories.detailText: Yahoo Sports is giving fans another way to play fantasy basketball with Perfect 5, a free-to-play game featuring each week's NBA on Prime doubleheader. The rules are simple: pick five players, stay within a $15 budget and rack up fantasy points through scoring, rebounds, assists, defensive stats and 3s. Friday's slate features the 76ers at Cavaliers (7:30 p.m. ET) and Trail Blazers at Lakers (10 p.m. ET). There's plenty of star power, but the key to building a competitive lineup is finding the right matchups and the values in the $1 tier. Using RotoWire's data and Yahoo projections, I ran 20,000 simulations of the slate. I'm paying up for Luka Dončić and leaning on two $4 bigs with great setups. Here's my lineup: My Perfect 5 lineup Player Team Salary Proj. pts Luka Dončić Lakers $5 50.14 Evan Mobley Cavaliers $4 42.46 Walker Kessler Lakers $4 37.90 Sidy Cissoko Trail Blazers $1 17.58 Meleek Thomas Cavaliers $1 12.00 Total $15 160.08 In my sims, this group averaged 160.08 fantasy points and finished in the top 1% of the field 21.7% of the time, the best rate of any lineup I tested. Luka Dončić – PG, Los Angeles Lakers – ($5, 76% picked) The chalkiest pick in the pool feels necessary because he's been one of the best, if not the best, players to start the season. Dončić is averaging 38.5 points, 8.2 rebounds, 8.0 assists and 5.9 3s, and he's gone for 40+ points in three straight games. Portland is middle of the pack against point guards, but when a guy is as hot as Luka, with a usage rate north of 40%, you play 'em. He was in the single best lineup in 55% of my simulations, more than any other player. Portland beat the Lakers 136-129 in L.A. on Oct. 27, even though Luka went for 41 points, 9 assists and 6 3s. He'll want this one back. Lock him in. Evan Mobley – PF, Cleveland Cavaliers – ($4, 12% picked) Mobley is projected for 42.46 fantasy points at $4, within about a point of Donovan Mitchell, whose salary is $5. He's putting up 18.8 points, 8.2 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.3 blocks, while hitting 2.1 3s a night. The matchup is neutral (Philly ranks 19th in fantasy points allowed to power forwards), and his usage has ticked up to 23.6% over the last three games. Jarrett Allen is questionable with a right knee contusion, after leaving Monday's contest after just seven minutes. If Allen sits, Mobley soaks up even more of the paint work against a light Philly frontcourt. At 12% picked, he's still the best combination of value and leverage on the slate. Walker Kessler – C, Los Angeles Lakers – ($4, 12% picked) Portland gives up 60.4 fantasy points per game to centers, the second-most in the league and about eight more than average. He's putting up 14.4 points, 10.2 rebounds and 2.7 blocks per night. I originally had Deni Avdija in this spot, but the matchups flipped it. The Lakers are one of the toughest defenses against small forwards, while Kessler gets one of the league's softest frontcourts. Now Kessler grades out better, and he's picked at the same 12% rate. Avdija is still a fine pivot if you'd rather have his playmaking, and that version of this lineup was a close second. Sidy Cissoko – SF, Portland Trail Blazers – ($1, 41% picked) Cissoko is the most popular non-Luka pick on the board. He's projected for 17.58 fantasy points at a $1 salary; I think he might be the best points-per-dollar mark on the slate. While the matchup isn't great (the Lakers are 26th in fantasy points allowed to small forwards), his minutes have held to around 21 a night. Trusting the math here, as he showed up in the optimal lineup in 45% of my sims. Meleek Thomas – SG, Cleveland Cavaliers – ($1, 14% picked) Here's where I'm going against Yahoo projections. Thomas is projected for only 12.00 fantasy points: that's too low. Over the last three contests, he's averaging 13.0 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.0 assist and 2.6 3s, which works out to roughly 21 fantasy points. His minutes match his production: he played 22.3 minutes over that span with a 25.4% usage rate. He was listed with right foot soreness on a recent injury report, so give it a look before tip. I'd originally pegged Kentavious Caldwell-Pope as the safe swap, but his minutes have dropped to 21, 13 and 18 in his last three, so I'm sticking with Thomas. How close is that to the max? Not quite. Using Yahoo's projections, the highest-scoring possible lineup is Dončić, Mobley, Jaylen Brown, Cissoko and Caldwell-Pope at 163.64 fantasy points. Mine comes in 3.56 points behind it. Player Team Salary Proj. pts Luka Dončić Lakers $5 50.14 Evan Mobley Cavaliers $4 42.46 Jaylen Brown 76ers $4 39.31 Sidy Cissoko Trail Blazers $1 17.58 Kentavious Caldwell-Pope 76ers $1 14.15 Total $15 163.64 The max lineup is a good build. It averaged nearly 164.0 points in my sims and finished in the top 1% about 13% of the time. Brown is a strong play, since Cleveland gives up the fifth-most fantasy points to small forwards. The weak spot is Caldwell-Pope and his shrinking minutes. The other problem is that everyone reading the same projections gets to this exact five, and it's the chalkiest high-projection build. In a game where you're trying to finish top-three against the whole Yahoo community, tying a bunch of people doesn't help much. Swapping Brown for Kessler and Caldwell-Pope for Thomas gives up 3.56 projected points but buys better matchups and more separation. You can start building your Perfect 5 roster for Friday's slate now , including going up against me in my Perfect 5 group . Good luck!

stories.title: Steph Curry earns ‘healthy monetary value’ from Klay Thompson
stories.summary: The matchup between the Warriors and Heat wasn't the only showdown this week with stakes for the Splash Brothers.
stories.detailText: Steph Curry and Klay Thompson squared off Thursday night for the eighth time in opposing uniforms. But it was a matchup earlier in the week that really got their competitive juices flowing. A few days before Curry led the Warriors to a comeback win over Thompson’s Heat, he notched another victory via the former teammates’ collegiate proxies. In a battle of Splash Brother alma maters, Davidson opened its season Monday night with a win over Washington State. “There was a healthy monetary value to that,” Curry quipped after Golden State’s 120-100 win . Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry, left, talks with Miami Heat guard Klay Thompson after an NBA game Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, in San Francisco. AP Photo/Tony Avelar Thompson confirmed that he most definitely heard from Curry after his Cougars took a 76-61 home loss to the Wildcats. In fact, that was all he heard leading into their own showdown. “The only conversations we’ve had are Davidson beating the Washington State Cougars and me getting the best end of that bet,” Curry said. “It actually snuck up on me. I knew the schedule, but the day before, I texted him, just, ‘It’s a great day in basketball history that the Wildcats are headed up to the Palouse to play his team.’ … Glad I came out on the right side.” A few days later, Curry came out on top again. Golden State fell behind by double digits in the first half for the fourth consecutive game but pulled out its sixth win in a row. Curry finished one shy of his fourth straight 30-point game. “What Steph’s doing,” Thompson said, “I might not have appreciated it as much as his teammate because I got to see it every night so it became normal, but to see it as an opponent, it’s incredible, especially that he’s nearing 40 and moves like a young athlete.” Stephen Curry (30) of the Golden State Warriors handles the ball against Klay Thompson (11) of the Miami Heat on Nov. 5, 2026, at Chase Center in San Francisco. NBAE via Getty Images Thompson, averaging 24.7 over his previous three games, was contained to 11 points on 3-of-10 shooting. He had been 19-for-36 from 3 over his past three games but drained only two of his seven attempts from distance, including an air ball on his contested first heave. In a twist on their previous matchups, the old Splash Brothers ended up defending each other for a good portion of the game. Thompson drained one of his 3s on Curry and picked up another three points at the foul line after getting Curry to bite on a pump fake. Only two of Curry’s 19 attempts came against Thompson. He beat him on one drive to the basket with an up-and-under, and Thompson got the upper hand on the other with a block. Klay Thompson #11 of the Miami Heat shoots against Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors in San Francisco on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. Getty Images “It’s still surreal playing against him,” Curry said. “It’s always gonna be that way cause we’ve gone through so many battles together. And it’s kind of cool even at this stage to guard him. “You’ve been on the other side of it for so long, so there’s an appreciation there. I think mostly it’s just an excitement of the fact that we’re still able to have battles. You know that every one that you get is one closer to the end. So you try to appreciate it even though there’s definitely a competitive spirit out there.” Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors and Klay Thompson #11 of the Miami Heat look on during a game, Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, in San Francisco. NBAE via Getty Images Still, the loss could only sour the night so much. “It still feels special every time,” Thompson said after his fifth trip back, “especially receiving the love from the fanbase and seeing people that I spent years with. It’ll always feel like home. … “It was fun, really fun. Steph’s super crafty, still to this day. It felt good to block his shot. He made a great up and under on me. He had an incredible night.” Thompson lamented Miami’s tough travel schedule, playing at Golden State a night after knocking off the Clippers in double overtime. Thompson’s corner 3 at the buzzer sealed the win. Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors and Klay Thompson #11 of the Miami Heat look on during a game at Chase Center in San Francisco on Nov. 5, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Warriors coach Steve Kerr said that he had been watching live. Curry was tuned in, too. “I texted Draymond [Green] right after,” Curry said. “Just told him Killa Klay. It’s always great to see him having fun but then you obviously wanted to come in and shut his water off tonight.”

stories.title: Doc Rivers Says Giannis Antetokounmpo Was 'Yo-Yoing' On Trade Request From Bucks
stories.summary: Doc Rivers has offered a candid look at Giannis Antetokounmpo's exit from the Milwaukee Bucks. stories.title: LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it
stories.summary: LeBron James took fan interaction to a whole new level on Monday night.
stories.detailText: LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James is one of kind in so many ways. What he did Monday night might be the cherry on top. In the third quarter of the Sixers’ 126-107 victory over the Bulls, James decided he’d take fan interaction to a whole new level. He helped himself to a fan’s red wine. James looked for a transition pass from Tyrese Maxey, who snagged a rebound. James was behind the pass and his momentum took him into the stands, where he disappeared for a few moments. It wasn’t until another angle was shown on replay that we could see what actually went down in the darkness of the seats. James didn’t hold back giving reporters a play-by-play. “I spilled some of his wine,” he said postgame. “I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine. So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm and how good it was. It was alright.” Troy Clemons – the Sixers fan whose drink spilled – explained his perspective on the interaction with James to Kris Rhim of ESPN. “[I was] walking to my seat … LeBron crashed into me, he grabbed me, he said ‘My bad,’ my drink spilled everywhere. He took my drink from me and he basically just took a sip of it, gave it back and ran back on the [court].” Did he keep the cup? “At the end of the day he’s another man like me,” Clemons said. “I mean he’s LeBron, but at the end of the day, I threw that cup in the trash. And it’s nothing up with him, I just got a fresh drink though.” It should be noted that players are not supposed to drink from fans’ cups, but it’s rare for the NBA to fine someone for a spontaneous interaction such as this. In 2019, a similar thing happened when Mike Scott tumbled into the Bucks’ court-side seats. The Sixers star jokingly took a sip of a fan’s beverage and the NBA opted not to fine him. Time will tell if James has the same fate. If nothing else, an interaction like this just shows how much fun James seems to be having. The 24-year veteran noted the importance of finding joy in the game as he grinds through the season. “It’s a long marathon. And if you don’t find ways to have fun throughout it, even though you’re working and even though you’re locked in, then it could wear on you. So for me, especially at this point in my career, being able to just appreciate the moments, the small moments, these fans are great to us. We try to be great to them as well. By playing the game the right way, playing the game hard and then also just being showmen as well, it was a great game for us.” Head coach Nick Nurse also weighed in on the 41-year-old’s mindset coming into the season. “This summer I think he probably stated publicly that he wanted to go some place and have some fun playing. He loves the game, [it’s his] 24th year. It’s a group of guys, like I keep saying, that have been super focused in the intent of playing the right way. I think he’s a big part of that.” The vibes are high. It’s difficult for them not to be. With Monday’s win against the Bulls, the Sixers are 7-1 and lead the Eastern Conference. They’ve won four in a row and the only team they’ve lost to is the Pistons. The Sixers will face them on Wednesday to start a three-game road trip.

stories.title: ‘I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers
stories.summary: Brown is complementing Philadelphia’s stars, attacking the glass and setting a "non-negotiable" defensive standard during the Sixers’ 7-1 start.
stories.detailText: ‘I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Jaylen Brown has spent the opening weeks of the season describing the Sixers as a work in progress. He offered a similarly humble perspective Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena. His performance, however, provided the clearest look yet at how he can influence this group while sharing the floor with the club’s other established stars. Brown finished with 25 points, 11 rebounds and five assists in the Sixers’ 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls. He shot 9 for 15 from the field, made four three-pointers and did not commit a turnover. Five of his rebounds came on the offensive end, an area Brown has emphasized while the Sixers continue piecing together their frontcourt rotation. “Just a mindset,” Brown said. “Just trying to create extra opportunities for my team. As we’re trying to patch together our fives and our front line, I try to make an extra contribution and emphasis on the glass.” Brown has also been careful about how he describes his place on a roster that already belonged to Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey. Maxey scored 15 of his 26 points in the fourth quarter Monday, continuing his torrid start to the season. He has led the Sixers in scoring while being the only starter to appear in all eight games. Brown is not interested in interrupting that. “Maxey’s been leading the way, 100 percent,” Brown said. “He’s been here. This is his team. Him and Joel have been here for a while, so the mindset has been to complement those guys. I’m finding my footing, but Maxey has been leading the way for sure.” Brown’s footing looked firm against Chicago. Beyond his scoring, he helped the Sixers control the glass, moved the ball within an offense that generated 23 assists during the first half and supplied the physicality Nick Nurse expects from him. “The dude is tough and he wins,” Nurse said. “I’ll take that all day long. The degree of difficulty on some of the shots he hit was really amazing. I thought he pounded the glass and got some key rebounds. Makes a lot of winning plays. Man, he’s a winner.” Brown spent the first 10 years of his career in Boston. He won a championship there, reached another NBA Finals and grew from a 20-year-old prospect into one of the league’s premier two-way wings. Moving into a new system alongside James, Embiid and Maxey was never going to be seamless. “I mean, he’s fitting in along with all of us,” James said. “We’re getting better and better. It’s not going to happen overnight. He spent his first 10 years in a system in Boston, in the city, so it’s going to take some adjustment. “It takes adjustment for him. It’s going to take adjustment for the rest of the guys that joined this franchise as well. But tonight was a great step.” James pointed to Brown’s “pressure, his shot-making ability, his rebounding ability” and his professionalism. Brown’s early influence has extended beyond his production. The Sixers entered Monday with one of the NBA’s best half-court defenses. Brown has been one of the group’s most persistent voices, stressing communication, preparation and attention to opposing players’ tendencies. “That’s the part that I care about the most as a group, not individually,” Brown said. “Having a mentality night in and night out, respecting your opponent, respecting the game, making sure that we are executing our coverages, we’re being clear in our communication and then we’re also taking away tendencies on a night-to-night basis. “Those things I just explained are over 50 percent of the battle.” Brown understands that maintaining those details across an 82-game schedule will require more than reminders. “A little bit of accountability,” he said. “You learn different guys require different things. How you communicate with each guy may be a little different, but accountability for sure and confrontation if need be. “The offense is going to be what it’s going to be, but our defense has got to be non-negotiable. That’s something I say all the time. Non-negotiable. You want to be a good team, defense is non-negotiable.” The Sixers showed both sides of their defensive potential Monday. They built a double-digit lead during the first half, allowed Chicago to score 36 points in the second quarter and then created separation after halftime. Philadelphia held the Bulls to 20 points in the third quarter before pulling away in the fourth. Brown did not celebrate their ability to raise their intensity after it slipped. “I don’t like that we have that,” he said. “It’s good that we have shown the potential, but we’ve got to keep that switch on. It doesn’t work like that where you just flip the switch. “It can catch up to us and it can bite us against a better team or on a night that we’re not being as crisp on offense. It can’t be a switch just because we’re playing a lesser opponent or whatever the case may be. We’ve got to make sure that mentality is from the beginning to end. Can’t skip any steps.” That urgency accompanies considerable optimism. Brown said the Sixers enjoy playing together. He loves when James grabs a rebound because “he’s like a quarterback,” capable of launching an outlet pass or immediately pushing the pace. The group is learning when to attack, when to move the ball and how to avoid hesitating in its effort to play unselfishly. “It’s a lot of talent, man,” Brown said. “We like each other, and we’re just kind of building that chemistry of how we can get this thing to a well-oiled machine. I think we’re taking steps forward every single day.” The Sixers are 7-1 despite Brown believing those steps remain incomplete. They have won close games, erased sizable deficits and received important contributions from different players. Brown’s performance Monday showed another version of how their pieces can fit. “We still have a long way to go to being a really, really solid, great team,” Brown said. “But we’ve been able to win some games. We started out the season great, 7-1, and you haven’t seen our best version yet. “That’s a good sign.”

stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1
stories.summary: The Sixers stayed hot Monday night, reaching 7-1 with a win over the Bulls.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers kept up their hot start to the season Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, reaching 7-1 with a 126-107 win against the Bulls. All five of the Sixers’ starters scored in double figures. Tyrese Maxey posted 26 points on 10-for-15 shooting and 11 assists. Jaylen Brown tallied a season-best 25 points and 11 rebounds. VJ Edgecombe’s 21 points were a new season high. LeBron James recorded 15 points, nine assists and seven boards. Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson had 24 points and seven rebounds. Joel Embiid (15 points, eight rebounds) had been listed as questionable with an official designation of “right foot plantar fascia injury management.” He sat out Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back for the Sixers’ win over the Hornets. “Plantar is a little bit of a come and go type of thing,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters pregame. “They’re just trying to manage it. It’s very painful, if you’ve ever had it. It can kind of come and go out of nowhere. So we’re just trying to manage the pain with that, be as smart as we can.” Nurse told reporters that Dominick Barlow is set to see a specialist Tuesday about the back injury that’s sidelined him to start the season. “He’s been on court a little bit … not a ton of moving around,” Nurse said. “I think they want to get to tomorrow’s appointment. Hopefully, it’ll be positive and we can get into his workouts a little bit.” The Sixers will begin a three-game road trip Wednesday when they visit the Pistons. Here are observations on their victory Monday: Edgecombe slamming away off the bat After Embiid blitzed a Bulls pick-and-roll, Maxey picked off Matas Buzelis’ hurried pass to get the Sixers rolling in transition and James jammed home the team’s first field goal. Edgecombe got a slam soon after James grabbed a defensive rebound and the Sixers again pushed the pace. The Sixers scored six quick fast-break points, leading the Bulls to burn an early timeout, and James’ long-distance feeds were a major asset. “If you’re open, he’s going to pass it,” Edgecombe said of James. “The main thing is just being ready. Tonight I had to run and go get ‘em. If you’re open and he sees you, he’s going to pass the ball.” Edgecombe had a dunk-heavy first quarter. He threw down his second when Dean Wade nabbed a steal and dropped off a typically selfless dish to the Sixers’ explosive second-year guard, whose slam put the team up 22-13. The Sixers have an abundance of dangerous options in the open floor, Edgecombe included. As he’s already shown with his continued clutch shotmaking, the 21-year-old won’t become anything resembling a non-factor offensively this year as a byproduct of the Sixers’ enhanced star power. Over the team’s first seven games, Edgecombe had averaged 11.3 points. He scored 11 in the first period on 5-for-5 shooting. More rough minutes for Bona Adem Bona missed a dunk early in the second quarter, which stung a bit more when Jalen Smith drilled a three-pointer seconds later. Bona remained the Sixers’ main backup center. He had a poor first-half stint overall amid a largely negative start to his third season. The 23-year-old big man played well in the Sixers’ victory over the Bucks , posting six points, 13 rebounds and three blocks. Outside of that, his season has been sparse on bright moments so far. It’s reasonable to wonder when Nurse might turn to alternatives like Jabari Walker, who played a good game Saturday in Charlotte, or try James again at the five. The Bulls outscored the Sixers by eight points in Bona’s first run, cutting their derficit to 40-38. Chicago went in front with a three by former Sixer Buddy Hield. The Sixers regained the advantage late in the second quarter. Maxey and James each were excellent as passers in the first half, combining for 14 assists and three turnovers. James fired the ball to Wade for a corner three that gave the Sixers a 60-52 lead. Sixers outclass Bulls Following a third-quarter Embiid fadeaway jumper and two James lay-ins, the Sixers were up 17 points. The Bulls cut the Sixers’ lead down to 11 points by the start of the fourth quarter. With Bona still struggling and on four fouls, Wade began the fourth at center. Bona then briefly spelled Wade before being whistled for his fifth foul and taking a seat. Embiid ultimately wasn’t needed for any of the fourth period and only logged 25 minutes. Embiid said postgame that he was not available to return to the action in the fourth and has been feeling his plantar fasciitis on the court. The seven-time All-Star’s health is clearly not close to 100 percent. “I was on a minutes restriction,” he said. “(The foot) has been going like that for the past few weeks. It’s painful. Just got to manage it. “If it flares up pretty bad, got to take a step back. We’ve been able to manage it, but it has its ups and downs.” The Sixers’ lead got as low as eight points, but Chicago did not shoot well enough from three-point range (26.3 percent) or have sufficient firepower to sustain a meaningful comeback run. The bottom line is the Sixers are in a different class than the Bulls, who fell to 1-6. As for the Sixers, they’ll wake up Tuesday morning at the top of the Eastern Conference standings. “You’ve got some of these nights where you kind of call them professional wins. …You look at the records and all that kind of stuff, but they have a lot of talent,” Nurse said. “A lot of these teams play a way that’s a little scary. It’s fast and it’s furious, lots of threes. … They’re going to keep coming at you, high-possession games. So they’re not easy games and I’m glad that we handled it professionally tonight.”

stories.title: Bona doubtful, no Sixers starters on injury report for Cavs game

stories.detailText: Bona doubtful, no Sixers starters on injury report for Cavs game originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers listed backup center Adem Bona as doubtful for their Friday night meeting with the Cavaliers. Bona’s official listing on the team’s Thursday evening injury report was “cervical spine sprain.” He played one of his better games so far this season Wednesday in the 8-1 Sixers’ win over the Pistons , slamming in two second-quarter dunks and posting five points, two rebounds, a steal and an assist in 15 minutes. Bona headed back to the Sixers’ locker room with 8:56 left in the fourth quarter. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters postgame that the 23-year-old big man had “neck soreness” after taking a hit. Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear) will remain out for the Sixers in Cleveland. The Sixers beat the 4-4 Cavs in dramatic fashion on Oct. 22, overcoming a 29-point deficit to win a wild home opener. If Bona were to miss Friday’s game, Jabari Walker would be the logical next name in line at center behind Joel Embiid. Notably, the Sixers included no starters on their injury report. Tyrese Maxey had an apparent late-game injury concern Wednesday night when he seemed to hurt his right hand on an intentional Detroit foul. stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double
stories.summary: The Sixers improved to 3-0 Saturday night by beating the Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season. Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards. The Sixers’ absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team’s matchup with the Pistons on Sunday. Here are observations on the Sixers’ victory Saturday: Wade debuts, Embiid starts in style Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James’ place. He’d missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain. The 3-and-D forward scored the night’s first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession. Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team’s offense in the early going. The Sixers’ seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man. Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead. One of Embiid’s assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter. Second-quarter struggles The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn’t enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter. Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run. Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn’t carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly. Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins’ three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead. The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they’d fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win. The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team’s transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game’s first 19 fast-break points. Star trio produces The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup. Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup. Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks’ odds of a road win. They’d all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter. Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers’ lead to 97-87. The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel’el Ware’s put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee’s deficit to 117-114. The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure. For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

stories.title: What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique
stories.summary: They play a brand of unselfish, team-first basketball you rarely see from a team loaded with stars.
stories.detailText: What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia They’re a team of superstars that don’t play superstar basketball. That’s the beauty of this 76ers team. They play a brand of unselfish team-first basketball you rarely see from a team loaded with stars. LeBron James is one of the two or three greatest players in NBA history, a four-time MVP, a four-time NBA champion, a 1 st -ballot Hall of Famer. Joel Embiid is a seven-time all-star, a former MVP, an Olympic gold medalist and a likely Hall of Famer. Jaylen Brown is a five-time all-star, an NBA champion, a career 20 points-per-game scorer. Tyrese Maxey is a two-time all-star, one of only two NBA guards averaging 27.0 points per game over the last four years. Four certified megastars on one team. And somehow they’ve figured out how to leave their egos at the front door and play smart, tough, disciplined team basketball, the style of ball you just never see on these superstar-laden teams. On offense, they patiently work the ball around, always looking for the open man or a positive matchup. You’ve got this bunch of big-name, high-priced All-Stars who are just as happy to pass the ball as shoot it. That never happens. The 76ers are sixth in the NBA in assists, and they’re one of only four teams with twice as many assists as turnovers. Smart, unselfish, patient, disciplined. When an all-timer like LeBron averages 7.3 assists per game that speaks volumes. LeBron is fifth in the NBA in assists per game among forwards, which is wild. You can see the joy on his face when one of his passes leads to a basket. When one of the greatest players in history has that mentality, it rubs off on everyone around him. Embiid hasn’t really got going yet on offense and still takes too many 3’s, but he’s also embraced the team-first mentality, and his 4.8 assists per game are more than one full assist above his career average and 4 th -most in the NBA among centers or forward-centers. And still one of the most dominating defensive players in the league. Brown is averaging 27.0 points, which you expect, but he’s also averaging 4.3 assists per game, significantly above his career average of 3.8 coming into the season. He’s fit in so well so fast you forget its his first season here. And what can you even say about Maxey? Just a beast. He’s averaging nearly 30 points per game but never wastes a possession, always makes the right decision with the ball in his hands and is still finding time to average 4.3 assists per game. With James, Embiid, Brown and Maxey, the 76ers are the only NBA team with four guys averaging at least 16 points and 4 assists per game. Only the Pacers, Magic and Raptors have three. But where we’re really seeing this group playing out of their minds is on the defensive end, where this bunch of all-stars, including two newcomers, has been astounding. The 76ers have the 2 nd -best defensive efficiency rating in the league, behind only the Pistons, who they play Wednesday night, and they’re allowing the 2 nd -fewest points in the league, also behind Detroit. Last year, they allowed 123 points per game through eight games. This year they’re at 111. They’re holding teams to 43 percent shooting from the field, 3 rd -best in the league and their lowest since 2011-12. Their 9.3 steals per game are 6 th -most. All five starters are among the top 25 players in the league in defensive rating – James is fourth, Embiid 11 th , Edgecombe 15 th , Maxey 22 nd and Brown 23 rd . How is that even possible? It’s rare to see superstar-caliber guys play as hard on the defensive end as the offensive end. Everybody on this team embraces it. They hustle, they work, they communicate and most importantly they commit to it. The biggest concern when the 76ers built this dream team was that it would be a team of individuals out for themselves, but the reality has been the opposite. In a very short period of time, they’ve learned how to play together. How to play for each other. And we haven’t even mentioned V.J. Edgecomb, who at 21 years old has figured out how to assimilate into this loaded lineup, never force anything, wait for his opportunities and make huge shots when he gets his turn. Edgecombe is at 12.7 points and 3.0 assists per game, and his numbers are understandably down a bit from last year, but if that bothers him it sure doesn’t show. And the role players – Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Jabari Walker – have each adopted the same ego-free style of basketball, supporting the starters however they need to. Nick Nurse deserves a ton of credit for getting this bunch to play this brand of hoops. It’s not easy to get any NBA player to put team goals ahead of individual goals. But he’s got Hall of Famers and all-stars doing it and having a blast along the way. They all seem to love playing basketball the right way and they seem to love playing together. The 76ers are 7-1 and looking like a real threat to win the East, and they’re doing it by playing the game the right way. By committing to each other and not themselves.

After starting off the season with a couple of losses, the Silver and Black have won their next six, steadily climbing up the standings. Even when things don’t go well, San Antonio has been able to prevail. In the matchup against the Mavericks on Wednesday, the Spurs shot 36 three-pointers and made just five of them. Only a handful of times in league history has a team shot so poorly at that volume and won. And the poor shooting was only part of the issues. The bench got outscored by 28 points, and only four players cracked double digits in scoring. So how did the Silver and Black keep the streak going? Because they have Victor Wembanyama. Wemby had arguably the best game of his career, finishing with 52 points, 24 rebounds, and eight blocks. The Spurs outscored Dallas by 23 points when he was on the floor in a one-point win. He was everywhere on defense, deterring or swatting shots. His jumper was off, as it was the case for the entire team, but he made an absolute killing in the paint, where no Maverick could stop him. Wemby willed the team to a win with not much help from others, which is something that only true superstars can do. Hopefully, it won’t take such a Herculean effort from The Alien to secure the win against the bottom-dwelling Kings. Sacramento is having a rough season in which injuries have made a bad roster look more inept than anticipated. The Spurs already made easy work of them in a previous matchup this season, dominating early and cruising to a blowout win. The same outcome seems likely, but San Antonio will need to show the appropriate fear and not assume that their opponent will just roll over or that talent alone will get them another victory. San Antonio Spurs ( 6 -2) vs. Sacramento Kings (1-7) November 6th, 2026 | 9:00 PM CT Watch: DAZN | Listen: WOAI (1200 AM) Spurs injuries: Tobias Harris (calf) — Out, Jayden Quaintance (knee) — Out Kings injuries: Ben Simmons (Achilles) — Out, Keegan Murray (ankle) — Out, Maxime Raynaud (knee) — Out What to watch for: Can the bench contribute? The decision to insert Dylan into the starting lineup has been going well enough so far that reverting it wouldn’t make sense, at least at this point, but it has had an impact on the second unit. The Spurs’ bench ranks 27th in the league in points scored per game and 29th in assists per game. Simply put, there’s very little shot creation and firepower outside of the starting unit. The offensive struggles wouldn’t be a problem if San Antonio were bringing defensive specialists off the bench, but that’s simply not the case. Keldon Johnson has always been a subpar defender despite always bringing effort. Julian Champagnie struggles with quick perimeter players and is getting exposed often, as he can’t keep his man in front of him and has to funnel them to Luke Kornet, having a bad year so far, instead of Victor Wembanyama. Since the starting unit has so much talent, the Spurs have been able to win games despite lacking quality depth, but a game against a weak opponent on the first night of a back-to-back would be a perfect opportunity for the subs to shine and lighten the load of the starters. Keep Acuff Jr. inefficient One of the few bright spots of the Kings’ season has been the play of their prized rookie, Darius Acuff Jr. The seventh overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft leads all first-year players in scoring (25.6 a game) and assists (seven a game), and even on a bad team, looks like a true building block for the future — the type of offensive engine that could eventually lead a good attack. The big issue for the soon-to-be 20-year-old has been efficiency. Acuff has the green light in Sacramento, which is helping him put up the great raw numbers mentioned above, though they can feel a little empty at times. He’s shooting just 40 percent from the floor and 31 percent from beyond the arc while turning the ball over often. In Sacramento’s last game, he scored 22 points, but it took him 24 shots to get there. In the matchup with the Spurs from earlier in the season, he had 19 points on 20 shots. Since the Kings’ defense is abysmal, the only way for them to beat good teams is to outscore them. Veteran starters Zach LaVine, Domantas Sabonis, and De’Andre Hunter will likely do their job on the offensive end while Malik Monk is expected to do the same off the bench. But Acuff Jr. is the big X-Factor. If he puts up big numbers but isn’t efficient, Sacramento won’t likely be able to keep up with a superior opponent. A must-win for the midseason tournament The Spurs will play their first game of the Emirates NBA Cup. They will battle the Kings, Lakers, Warriors, and Trail Blazers in the West’s Group C. Sacramento is clearly the worst team of the bunch, so beating them is a must if the Silver and Black, which played in the finals against the Knicks in the previous edition of the competition, are hoping to advance. If you’d like to, you may follow along with the game on our Twitter profile (@poundingtherock) or visit our Game Thread!

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images At some point between the end of the ‘21 season and the start of the ‘22 season, I made a pact with myself: no more first quarters . You have to understand, these were dark times to be a Spurs writer. And yes, I know, as a fan myself, that those years were no more of picnic for the average fan than they were for me, but still. There’s just something about watching a beating and then having to write about it that feels vaguely abusive, especially when some of your favorite people are still involved. Having to watch Gregg Popovich lose like that…I felt like a journalist covering Muhammad Ali’s last fights. It didn’t matter how valiant he was, how much he tried to make something out of nothing — it just seemed kind of dirty to watch at all. We all knew what he was doing, of course. But watching a worthy sacrifice doesn’t make it any easier. I still get misty-eyed when the Iron Giant tells Hogarth Hughes not to follow him (as if he could) before rocketing from the ground into space, and meeting the falling arc of a nuclear warhead. There’s a reason I don’t watch the movie all the time. It would be fairly masochistic of me to do so. But there are 82 games in a season, and someone has to cover them. As a writing staff, you take some solace in the knowledge that you’re all in this together. You’re all having to write about it. You’re all having to dig for silver linings. And that (for this site) you’re all doing it out of some (possibly misplaced) sense of love for the team, and the sport, and the readers who are just about as miserable as you are. But I just could not watch first quarters anymore. Not in real time. It’s one thing to know that the Titanic is sinking; to be thrown into the middle of the chaos and do your best to make sense of it. It’s another thing altogether to watch the ship headed towards the ice-burg in the darkness. To hear the godawful scraping and know what it means. To have been watching the journey for years, and completely run out of ways to spin it. It had to have been a very conscious decision on James Cameron’s part to make that movie a romance. How else could you get people to watch it? The wreck just cannot be the main course. I couldn’t convince myself to watch the game at all if I started with the first quarter. The Spurs would either start taking their beating from the onset, or worse, soar to an early lead that we all knew wouldn’t last. So I decided that I would start watching during the second quarter, finish the game, and then watch the beginning. It was so much easier to bear when you already knew how it would end. Especially when the Spurs did miraculously pull off the win. You could go back and break down how the positive momentum started, with the empty but understandable hope that there might be something algorithmic in those 12 minutes that could be reverse-engineered and employed more regularly. And even the sting of defeat didn’t smart as much when you were able to initially avoid the fool’s gold of productive opening minutes. Hell, sometimes it was even a little funny when you encountered the Spurs finding a way to lose the opening frame that you’d never even considered. (Even though the Spurs won the game, I don’t think I’ll ever forget Jakob Poeltl picking up 2 fouls in the first 96 seconds of the Lakers game in 2022 that tied Pop with Don Nelson.) Lately, though, I’ve been forced to reconsider my first-quarter policy, and the reason is pretty obvious: Victor Wembanyama is just too fun to be put on the back-burner in any capacity. It was a sensible policy when the losses were piling up. Sometimes it still is. But frustration with a contender-caliber team starting slowly is simply not enough to deprive myself of the immediacy of the joy provided by the most insane fusion of Hakeem Olajuwon, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, and Wilt Chamberlain imaginable. Wemby just had the first *official* 50 point, 20 rebound, 8 block game in NBA history (and the first 50/20/10 in the non-assist category if you combine his steals and blocks), in his 8th game of his 4th season, and he’s the same age that Wilt was as a rookie! Chamberlain didn’t even peak until he was 25! That’s the territory we’re in. That’s the conversation. And that’s in spite of existing in the era of injury and rest management. In spite of the fact that Wemby’s doing it on a team that’s good enough to have already made the Finals. In spite of playing in an era where blocks are harder to come by, and strategic scouting and game-plans are another level, and players are (pretty successfully) bombing away from long range. In spite of an out-of-whack jumper that’s converting at about 28% outside of 10 feet. Having chugged a 16oz energy drink during my late dinner before the game in an attempt to battle the somnolent rigidities of middle-age, I found myself doing the same ‘fighting the urge to pee’ dance that my child still breaks out every now and then, as I tried to hold out til the end of the half. Smelling weakness through the television screen like a shark loose in a blood bank, Wemby proceeded to block three shots in roughly 13 seconds , as if to say: are you sure that you want to miss this? I can’t remember the last time I almost wet myself over basketball, or a more satisfying pee at the half. There’s plenty of negative things I could say about the game. I don’t know that I’ve ever seen this team shoot that badly as a whole. Even Julian Champagnie and Devin Vassell couldn’t buy a shot. There’s no reason it should have been that close with such a performance out of Wembanyama. The bench’s defense looked like it had been coordinated by Wile E. Coyote and the Acme Corporation, and they put up a total of ten points in their relief of the starters. Carter Bryant and Tarris Reed somehow got no minutes on a night in which it couldn’t have been more clear that a shakeup was needed. Even De’Aaron Fox’s previously next-level show of efficiency took the wrong turn at Albuquerque. This was a bad game, if we’re being honest. A real stinker. And yet I can’t find the animosity within me to make this the all-around feel-bad roast that it should be, because, as I’ve said so many times over the last year, it just did not matter. This should have been one of those games where I had to go back and break down the first quarter in a state of rage. It should have been. But I just don’t have it in me to despair the undespairing. Through it all, Wemby was completely unshaken. Understandably, so were his teammates. In their shoes, I think I’d feel the same way. I don’t love that they frittered away lead after lead. I don’t like it as a trend, and I don’t like it as reminder. But I think it’s easy to forget that we don’t live in that place were I can’t stand to watch the first quarter anymore, and that by resigning myself to that policy of the past, I’d be getting in the way of my own happiness. You can’t protect yourself from pain without also protecting yourself from rapture. I think sometimes, in both life and basketball, we have a way of forgetting that. I can tell you everything they did wrong. I can rant and rage with the best of them, and sound my barbaric yawp over the roofs of the world. I can tell you that they were saved anyway, undeservingly . Give me a better story than that, I dare you. Takeaways I don’t have a lot of nice things to say about this game, but man has Wemby really taken to the responsibility of attacking the rim this season. Right now he and Giannis are the only players in the NBA averaging 7+ Rim FGs and 8+ Paint FGs made per game. And Wemby’s actually doing it more ways than Giannis is, as the only player in the league averaging 5+ points as the P&R Roll Man, 4+ Points off of Cuts, and 4+ points In Transition, per game . If his jumper starts heating up, we’re going to see even crazier numbers than we did last night. Which is insane when you consider that he’s 4th in the league in scoring with a jumper finds the bottom of the bucket about 1/4th of time right now. It’s been a bit of an uncomfortable fit for Stephon Castle when all three guards are on the court at the same time, and he seems to have been asked to serve as more of an off-ball shooter because of that, but when the need arises, he always seems to find an extra gear. I know many are hoping that the addition of Tobias Harris forces some rotation adjustments, but I will say, Castle is getting the open shots, and he’s not shrinking from the challenge. He’s shooting 32% from three now, but if he starts hitting those, that lineup might really morph into something scary, because everything will open up on the inside, and Wemby’s already mutilating the rim as it is (and Harper’s been slouch, either). And as much as I think Harris will be a boon to the team, I’d secretly prefer to see that happen instead. Though Fox had probably his most inefficient night of the season on the offensive end, he’s still the only player in the NBA creating 15+ Assist Points Per Game, with a 2-1 Assist-to-Turnover Ratio, while also sporting a 65+ True Shooting Percentage, which is crazy when you see all the names that miss the mark. But, just as importantly, he’s been outstanding on the defensive end, and it showed in the clutch last night when he kept the still-lethal (and long-time Spurs killer) Kyrie Irving off-balance just enough to that his attempt at a game-winning bucket. To have lost a game with Victor playing like that would have felt catastrophic, so he’d be next in line for the game ball, in my mind. stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_miltonstarting_261105","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"477944","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_miltonstarting_261105","genre":"News","guid":"nbc_pft_miltonstarting_261105","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"Philadelphia Eagles","title": "Eagles give Milton an opportunity against Giants","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/eagles-give-joe-milton-an-opportunity-against-giants-in-week-9","availableDate":"2026-11-05T13:45:13Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} How do you know when a football coach is lying? If he's good at it, you don't. Because they all do. Particularly in so-called "must-lie" situations. There's an art to it. A way to conceal a lie with another lie. On Friday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni opted not to lie about the fact that he lied on Monday when he told reporters that quarterback Tanner McKee would not be benched. " Tanner’s our guy ," Sirianni said. "We're not making any changes there." On Wednesday, the Eagles made a change there, elevating Joe Milton over McKee. The move was announced after Sirianni had his midweek media availability, which prevented him from being asked questions about the change in position from "Tanner's our guy" to "Tanner's not our guy." On Friday, Sirianni finally faced the music regarding his comments from Monday. In lieu of coming up with an explanation premised on the idea that what he said was true when he said it and circumstances changed, Sirianni surprisingly admitted that he wasn't telling the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth to reporters and, in turn, the fans. "I was going to hold onto that as long as I possibly could, every second, every minute," Sirianni said. "Again, I'm not real shy with you guys. I'm going to tell you what I want to tell you guys. I respect the job that y'all have to do, but I'm going to tell you what I want to tell you guys because I'm always going to protect the team first and foremost. "Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. I know there's a lot of interest in everything that you all want to hear, the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games, do everything we can do to help win football games, protect the guys here on this football team, and handle everything that I can inside." In an industry where the truth is only told when it's coincidental to strategic interests, it's jarring that Sirianni told the truth that he was lying. It would have been easy to say, "We took a more careful look at the situation after Monday." Or, even more simply, "We changed our mind. Shit happens." Instead, Sirianni opted to say, essentially, "Bullshit happens." Instead of bothering to concoct a cover story regarding his lie, he said, essentially, "Yeah. I lied. I'll do it whenever I feel like I have to." That's the most important thing to remember. Coaches lie whenever they feel like they have to. Despite that fact, reporters and fans routinely take their words at face value, swallowing the bullshit while saying, "Thank you, sir, may I have another?" So thank you, Nick, for making my job a little easier. In my first week of law school, one of the professors said, "The most important thing I can do for you is to give you a good crap filter." Because crap is everywhere. Usually, the people spewing it don't admit it. When they do, it provides a tangible reminder as to whatever they say in the future. For Sirianni, that's the most problematic aspect of his decision to tell the truth about lying. There's now an "Exhibit A" to which anyone and everyone can point as to anything and everything he says when assessing whether he's being straight with reporters and, in turn, with fans.

stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up against the New York Giants at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2025 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final injury report of the week on Friday in advance of their Week 9 game against the New York Giants. The Eagles ruled six players OUT: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Michael Carter II, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Smith and Wicks haven’t been able to play since Week 6. With them and Covey out, the Eagles are down to four wide receivers on the active roster: Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, and Elijah Moore. Look for Lemon to see the most targets. It’ll be interesting (a very relative term in this case) to see how new starting quarterback Joe Milton jibes with this group. Campbell is missing his second straight start. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. will get the nod next to Zack Baun. MC2’s absence leaves the Eagles thinner at safety and nickel cornerback than usual. Covey being out puts Cooper DeJean in position to return punts. The Eagles will be without their top backup cornerback on the outside with Jones not playing. The Eagles ruled one player QUESTIONABLE: Tanner McKee. McKee was full in practice on Wednesday with a chest injury. He was then limited on Thursday and Friday due to a rib injury. stories.title: Lions, Dolphins Week 9 injury designations: Lions rule out 5 starters

stories.detailText: Detroit Lions center Cade Mays (64) warms up ahead of the game between Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions (5-2) and Miami Dolphins (1-6) have declared their Week 9 injury designations, and the Lions will be missing multiple starters, including one on offense, three on defense, and one not yet cleared from his injury list—all of which we knew ahead of time, based on coach Dan Campbell’s comments throughout the week. Let’s look at Friday’s practice report and get you up to date on what we know. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . Ruled OUT C Cade Mays (ankle) — Preparing for Juice Scruggs to start EDGE DJ Wonnum (concussion) LB Jack Campbell (neck) CB D.J. Reed (hip) S Kerby Joseph (knee, PUP) — Days remaining in injury evaluation clock: 11 Mays is dealing with a low ankle sprain, which typically keeps players out at least a week, and potentially as long as a month, so him being ruled out of this game was expected. How quickly he recovers is still to be determined, but the Lions have been highly fortunate to have Juice Scruggs stepping into the starting center role, and they’ve been planning on him starting since the beginning of this week. Wonnum is still working through the NFL’s concussion protocols and won’t be able to return in time for this game. With head injury recovery times varying by individual, it’s unclear how long he will need before he is cleared. Second-round rookie Derrick Moore is expected to increase his role in Wonnum’s absence, and Campbell is seeing improvement: “It was unfortunate we lost Wonnum, but yet, now (Moore) gets more reps. And the reps that he got are valuable, man. There’s no way to duplicate real in time game reps against good opponents and you see growth, you see growth. I saw growth in practice yesterday. So, the more he plays, the better he’s going to get. And we love where he’s going right now.” Jack Campbell continues to improve, per Dan Campbell, but he should be considered out indefinitely until otherwise clarified. “Jack continues to improve, which is all great news,” Dan Campbell said on Friday. Reed said he felt good in the locker room following the game, but he was not cleared to practice this week and will miss this game. Campbell noted that he’s very confident with the team’s depth: “(Ennis) Rakestraw is getting better. Rock (Ya-Sin) looks healthy and is playing good football. (Roger) McCreary, too. So, I just feel like these guys are starting to play pretty good football for us. And (Khalil) Dorsey, man, Dorsey’s contributing in a big way. So, I like where we’re at and it’s really a pretty depthwise, it’s a pretty strong room. So yeah, I don’t like the though of not having Reed, but at the same time, I’m encouraged. I’m encouraged. I think we’ll be OK here.” Joseph is looking “better than anticipated,” according to safeties coach Jim O’Neil, but Campbell made it clear earlier in the week that the plan was to keep him out for another game, then continue to ramp up his participation levels next week, as he nears a return. “It’s been great. Two weeks ago, it was classroom work, where we were really locked in. Then it was walkthrough and individual. Yesterday was his first team practice and he looked a lot better than what I anticipated him looking (like). So it was very encouraging. So now he’s gotta stack multiple days. He’s got to stack them, so today will be a big day for him, but he looked awesome yesterday at practice,” O’Neill said on Friday. Questionable RB Sione Vaki (ankle) — added to the injury report on Friday RB Jacob Saylors (neck) WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) Vaki was unexpectedly absent from Friday’s practice and has been given a questionable designation heading into this weekend’s game. Beyond that, the extent of his injury is unknown, and we may have to wait until Saturday—to see if he travels with the team—or even game time on Sunday, to find out his availability. Saylors has dealt with a neck injury for two weeks and couldn’t finish Week 7’s game against the Vikings because of it. Look for the Lions to be cautious in his return, but with Vaki also questionable, the Lions could end up with a depth issue at running back. St. Brown was injured in Week 7 but told the media on Thursday that, “I’m a little banged up, but I’ll be alright,” and is anticipating playing against the Dolphins. Not listed with an injury designation LB Amen Ogbongbemiga (toe) CB Rock Ya-Sin (cramps) S Brian Branch (concussion) Ogbongbemiga was estimated to have been a limited participant on Wednesday and a full participant after that, and with him not carrying an injury designation, he should be good to go, giving the Lions special teams work and linebacker depth. Ya-Sin dealt with cramps earlier in the week but still practiced in full each day. He’s potentially in line to challenge for a starting role this week with Reed sidelined. Branch is nearing the end of the NFL’s concussion protocol, and Campbell said he expects him to be cleared and ready to play on Sunday. “I think (Brian Branch) BB’s going to be good here. We’ll get through today, and I think we’ll be OK.” Dolphin s’ injury designations Coming soon.

stories.detailText: The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries Carolina’s injury report is scarier than many of last week’s Halloween costumes. Let’s start with the good news first. Veteran offensive lineman Brady Christensen has been progressing and looks like he will be active this week. He is officially listed as questionable. Provided he’s healthy, it will be up to the coaching staff to determine if — and which position — he ends up playing this week. The Panthers offensive line is a shambles right now and Christensen has the versatility to play all five positions. Here’s to hoping he’s both healthy and productive against the Broncos. Defensive tackle Bobby Brown is also trending in the right direction after missing last week’s game with a hand injury. He was a full participant in practice this week and doesn’t have an injury designation as of Friday’s practice. Now, the bad part. Three important contributors to the Panthers defense are in bad shape including outside linebacker Jaelen Phillips, cornerback Will Lee, and linebacker Bobby Okereke. They are all listed as out this week. On the offensive side of the ball, guard Damien Lewis missed last week’s game with a knee injury and is also out against the Broncos. Transactions Signed CB Jakorian Bennett to the practice squad Jakorian Bennett could help provide reinforcements to the Panthers’ bruised and bloodied cornerbacks room. He was originally a 2023 fourth-round pick by the Las Vegas Raiders. In two seasons in Sin City he appeared in 24 games with 11 starts, registering 58 tackles and an impressive 11 passes defended. After two solid seasons Raiders traded him before the 2025 season to the Philadelphia Eagles. He appeared in 11 games for Philly last year with seven tackles before suffering an injury and getting waived just a few days ago with an injury designation. Signed OT Da’metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad Speaking of battered and bruised units on the Panthers roster, the entire offensive line needs some reinforcement. This week the Panthers signed tackle Da’metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad. He entered the league this year as an undrafted free agent out of Syracuse and has spent some time with the Bills and Patriots before coming to Charlotte. He has yet to appear in an NFL game. Signed LB Mohamoud Diabate to the practice squad If the name Mouhamoud Diabate sounds familiar it’s because he’s had a decent NFL career in what is now his fifth season. He spent his first three seasons with the Cleveland Browns from 2023 through 2025 appearing in 46 games with 127 tackles. He had a career-high 70 tackles back in 2024. But his previously promising young career hit a detour last year when he joined the Tennessee Titans and appeared in only one game while bouncing around the practice squad. He now joins the Panthers practice squad with a decent amount of on-field experience. Releases: This week the Panthers also released CB Zion Childress LB Maema Njongmeta from the practice squad.

stories.title: Sources: Ravens trade 4th-, 7th-rounders to get Jacoby Brissett, 5th-round pick
stories.summary: The Ravens will acquire quarterback Jacoby Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick for a fourth-round pick in 2027 and seventh-round pick in 2028, sources told ESPN and NFL Network.
stories.detailText: The Baltimore Ravens have completed their trade for Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett , the teams announced Friday. The Ravens will acquire Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick for a fourth-round pick in 2027 and seventh-round pick in 2028, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. The teams were finalizing a trade to send Brissett to Baltimore ahead of the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday. The Ravens were in need of a quarterback after losing starter Lamar Jackson to a potentially season-ending thumb injury that will require surgery and backup Tyler "Snoop" Huntley to a turf toe injury. Sources had told Schefter and Rapoport on Wednesday that Huntley will miss the rest of the season. In the interim, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano started for the Ravens on Thursday, going 10-for-18 for 60 yards with two interceptions in the loss to the Jaguars. Baltimore (4-5) was held under 14 points for a fourth straight game, breaking a team record in futility. The Ravens also have lost by 20 or more points in three straight games for the first time in their 31-year history. Brissett had been benched this week by the Cardinals, who named Gardner Minshew II as their starting quarterback moving forward. Rookie Carson Beck was named the backup with Brissett as the third-stringer. Going back to Week 6 of the 2025 season, Brissett had started the past 20 games for the Cardinals before he was benched late in the third quarter of Sunday's 33-30 overtime victory over the Dallas Cowboys . Brissett asked for a trade Monday when coach Mike LaFleur called to tell him about the shake-up in the quarterbacks room, a source told ESPN. "I think it was a little bit of a perfect storm of a lot of things there," Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort said Friday. "Obviously, our game played out the way it did on Sunday, and then postgame, our discussions on how we were going to operate moving forward, and that continued into Monday morning." Over the past 20 games, Brissett ranked No. 1 in dropbacks, completions and attempts, third in passing first downs, fourth in completion percentage over expected, fifth in passing yards, and seventh in passing yards and broken sacks. He was sacked 62 times over that stretch, which is tied for the most in the NFL. "Have the utmost respect for Jacoby Brissett," Ossenfort said. "Going back to last year, what he did to stabilize a position that was in flux last year and the toughness and the leadership that he brought to that position, the professionalism, the way that he went about his job every day, took a lot of shots, kept getting up, a lot of respect for Jacoby." Before the looming trade to Baltimore, the Cardinals restructured Brissett's contract, converting $2.7 million of his remaining $5.4 million salary into a signing bonus, according to ESPN's Field Yates. The Ravens will owe Brissett a base salary of $2.43 million, and there are incentives in his deal to make additional money. Brissett will reunite with Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork, who held the same position last season with Brissett in Arizona. The two also worked together in 2022 with the Cleveland Browns . Baltimore placed Jackson on injured reserve before Thursday's game. He will miss at least three more games, but the Ravens have not given a definitive timetable on him. Asked after the game whether Jackson had surgery on his hand and whether he has a chance of returning this season, coach Jesse Minter replied, "I'm not going to speak on that." ESPN's Jamison Hensley and Josh Weinfuss contributed to this report.
