stories.title: How the 49ers plan to use DeForest Buckner with new look DL room
stories.summary: The Niners look to be getting multiple new defensive linemen into the mix this weekend.
stories.detailText: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 20: DeForest Buckner #99 of the Indianapolis Colts sacks Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs during the second quarter of an NFL football game on September 20, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are hitting the field on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, coming off a bye week, and they’ll have their new addition on the defensive line with them. Recently traded defensive tackle DeForest Buckner is set to make his 49ers return, marking his first game in San Francisco uniform since the 2019 Super Bowl. Buckner, 32, has long been known as a quality pass rusher with a unique size-length profile at 6’7, and will hope to add some of that to a young defensive tackle room that also includes Osa Odighizuwa. Now, the 49ers have their two veterans, along with rookie Gracen Halton and former undrafted free agent Sebastian Valdez as their top depth. With the Indianapolis Colts, Buckner had a top five snap count among defensive tackles this season. With the 49ers, that’ll hopefully drop as the 49ers rotate their linemen more. But, with Buckner and Odighizuwa both having familiarity playing as three-techniques, how will the 49ers use Buckner in his return? “We’ve done so many different things, moved people around,” defensive coordinator Raheem Morris said. “They have the ability to play three-technique. They have the ability to play nose. They have the ability to play four-eye, the ability to play on the edge. You’ve kind of seen these guys kind of move around all over the place, so I wouldn’t really put them in a bucket. “You’re talking about a guy with supreme talent. Those guys kind of can do whatever you ask them to do. Traditionally he’s been a three-technique around here, playing a huge role and doing some really good things. He’ll do a lot of the same thing. I’m a big believer in doing what people do really well and we’ll try to find out what he does really well again, implement them to what the guys have been doing and put those guys together and put them out there playing fast.” The 49ers have regularly been moving players around, kicking some of their bigger edges inside, while also creating different ways to rush the passer. The creativity should increase with Nick Bosa also trending to play, but it doesn’t seem like Morris is concerned with the usage. San Francisco has been without Bosa for a few weeks now, and their pass rush has struggled a bit as a result. Now, with him and Buckner both likely in the fold this week, what will that do for the defense? “I don’t know when it would be a bad time to get a guy like Buck,” Morris added. “It’s been a lot of fun to meet him the last couple of days and be around him and watch him practice and put him a part of it. Really feel like I’m further away from it than he is because of how long he spent here and the time that he spent here and how much he means to this organization and the people around him. “So, it’s been a lot of fun being around that guy and to have that whole unit being able to come back relatively healthy. To see these guys (Buckner and Bosa) probably for the first time altogether, I think altogether, for the first time this year, I think it’d be a lot of fun.” Now, the 49ers have two veterans in their defensive tackle room, which should only help in the development of younger guys like Mykel Williams, Halton, Valdez, Romello Height, and the rest of the room. “Buck’s done it at a very high level for such a long time,” Morris continued. “I don’t know if there’s anybody in this building that can’t pick something up from him. I just know how much, let’s just go with the ultimate leader in Fred [Warner] and [Dre] Greenlaw, how much respect those guys have for him. So when you’re talking about guys that have done a lot of really cool things at different positions that can learn from him, you can only imagine what the guys up front can get from him, just those guys being together. “Having Osa being a vet and then having Buck come in with some different perspective, different realities of what he’s been through and what he’s done. To be able to come back into the fold and really pick it back up and fit right back in with the guy that’s coached him, guys that he’s familiar with, whether it be the head coach or his position coach, I think is always a really good thing.” The Niners will kick things off against the Raiders this weekend as they look to start the second half of the season hot. We’ll get to see how Buckner looks returning to the 49ers, and whether the team still needs to make another move ahead of the deadline.

stories.title: Patience, professionalism paying off for NY Giants’ RB Devin Singletary
stories.summary: Singletary might be the last man standing on Sunday from the Giants’ initial four-man backfield.
stories.detailText: Devin Singletary | Getty Images New York Giants running back Devin Singletary was inactive from Weeks 3-5. In Weeks 1,2, and 6 — while the Giants were trying to figure out a workable backfield rotation — Singletary carried the ball only 13 times. Yet, there he was on the final play of overtime in Week 7 against the Houston Texans, the last man standing from what had been a four-man competition. An unhappy Najee Harris had been cut days before. Tyrone Tracy suffered a hamstring injury in the first half that would land him on IR. One play earlier, Cam Skattebo had injured his own hamstring on a career-best 42-yard run. So, it was Singletary left to take the handoff from J.J. McCarthy at the Texans’ 30-yard line in a tie game. Suddenly, he was in the secondary. Then, after a couple of nifty cuts, he was in the end zone and the Giants had won a game. In the post-game madness, a jubilant Singletary and head coach John Harbaugh landed in a heap on the ground. Harbaugh tackles Singletary after OT Win 🙌 Singletary gets tackled by his coach after game-winning TD pic.twitter.com/wHpduP4wOv — New York Post Sports (@nypostsports) October 25, 2026 Singletary said this week that “I still don’t know” if Harbaugh tackled him, or vice versa. “I think we just tripped,” Singletary said. “As Coach would say, it’s football joy. You go through a lot to be able to get to football joy. We were just so happy, so excited. He was telling me how much he loved me. I was telling him how much I loved him.” Singletary said there “was never no bad feelings” between himself and Harbaugh because of the eight-veteran’s lack of opportunities. Singletary, 29, understand that it was “business.” Of course Singletary, who has more than 1,100 carries and 5,000 NFL rushing yards, didn’t like not playing. He did appreciate Harbaugh’s honesty. “One thing I do respect about him, he kept it real with me. You don’t always see that in the league. That’s why I always got so much respect for him for that reason,” Singletary said. “It was just, this is what it is right now. I need you to stay patient and we’ll see how it plays out. Simple as that. “I was like, I appreciate that. Some people won’t even tell you that. They’ll just leave you there with no answers, with nothing.” It played out such that Singletary got to play the hero against the team he gained a career-high in rushing yards for in 2023. New York touchdown! Devin Singletary runs it in from 30 yards out with 7:25 left in overtime. NYG: 27 | HOU: 21 #NYGvsHOU #BigBlue #HTownMade pic.twitter.com/z8BoHAOp9m — NFL TD Bot (@nfltdbot) October 25, 2026 “I wouldn’t say frustrating,” Singletary said in reference to his lack of playing time. “It’s like, yes, part of it is how the game goes. It’s a lot of competition. It’s a deep backfield. But as far as being a pro, that’s me. That’s how I was brought up. “I’m going to always go about my business the right way. Stay ready, because when that opportunity comes, you want to be ready to seize the moment instead of being so mad or whatever it is, sad or whatever, and you can’t capture the moment when it’s here.” After the Texans game, Harbaugh said Singletary’s lack of playing time was “on me.” “We were looking for the formula, and Devin wasn’t — he was the odd man out for a number of weeks. Not because of anything he did or didn’t do, he just was the odd man out, and that’s exactly what I told him,” Harbaugh said. “He asked me, ‘what can I do?’ I said, ‘there’s nothing you can do, you’re doing everything you can do, and your time will come’. It was going to come. And look where it came, right there, and he came through.” Offensive coordinator Matt spoke this week about how appreciative he is of Singletary’s professionalism. “We went through the whole thing with the different running backs and four or five guys and he’s been here from day one, from OTA’s, and through training camp, through the season, wasn’t playing, wasn’t active. And he’d sit back in practice when he wasn’t playing and not say a word, but just be completely professional,” Nagy said. “And we talked, and we talked about great things happen to great people and I just think back to that Texans game, and when he scored that touchdown at the end, the discussions that we had in practice when he wasn’t playing, he never became negative, he never made it about him. He was as great of a professional player as there was, and look what happened. “And I think it’s a story for young kids, it’s a story for vets to be patient, to understand things happen for a reason and when he scored that touchdown, I couldn’t think but anything of how he handled himself the entire last five weeks. And we talked about it in the locker room, and I think for him, what a credit and we’re lucky to have him.” Baseball fans might recall the name Tommy Henrich, an outfielder/first baseman for the New York Yankees from 1937-1950. His nickname was ‘Old Reliable’. In a way, it is what Singletary has become for Harbaugh’s Giants. Now, with Tracy on IR and Skattebo perhaps unable to play Sunday against the Eagles, Singletary is likely to be the lead back. “I know what I can do. I want to be able to display that,” Singletary said. “We’ll see what this week brings, but yeah, I’m excited.”

stories.title: Rams' Myles Garrett to be activated from injured reserve, play vs. Commanders
stories.summary: Rams star pass rusher Myles Garrett is on track to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game at the Commanders.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES -- Rams outside linebacker Myles Garrett is expected to play Sunday against the Commanders "barring any sort of setbacks" with his knee injury, coach Sean McVay said Friday. McVay said the expectation is that Garrett as well as tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will be activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game. Both players returned to practice this week. The Rams are still working through how much Garrett will play, McVay said, adding that the pass rusher has "really done a great job in practice" this week. "He has progressed really well, made a tremendous impact in practice on Wednesday and Thursday [and] feels really comfortable with the game plan," McVay said. "And it's been great having him out there as well as Terrence." If Garrett is active as expected, he will play alongside defensive tackle Aaron Donald for the first time. Donald did not play in Week 1 -- Garrett's first and only game for the Rams so far -- while working his way back from retirement. "I think the offenses really have to pick their poison," Garrett said of playing with Donald. "Who's going to be freed up this play? And I think either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-one, so we'll have some fun." Garrett has been on injured reserve since undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September. He played in the Rams' season opener but said after the game that he was not 100% healthy. Garrett missed most of training camp while dealing with what McVay called knee irritation at the time. There wasn't one moment where Garrett injured his knee, he said, but it "just cascaded" and then got worse as he played against the San Francisco 49ers . "There were just some hitches in my gait," Garrett said. "There were just things I was dealing with mechanically that just only continued to evolve, or I guess worsen, as I played more throughout that game." Ferguson has missed five games after spraining his ankle in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos . The Rams traded for Garrett this offseason, sending two-time Pro Bowl pass rusher Jared Verse and three draft picks, including a first-round selection in 2027, to the Cleveland Browns . Garrett was the NFL Defensive Player of the Year in 2025 after setting the single-season sack record with 23 for the Browns. McVay said cornerback Trent McDuffie -- another big offseason addition for the Rams -- would not practice again Friday and will be questionable for Sunday's game. McDuffie injured his back in Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers .

stories.title: Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson affected by neurological symptoms
stories.summary: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson said tests have come back positive after he suffered "unexplained neurological symptoms" that remain "unknown and unexplainable."
stories.detailText: FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson said he recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms" and that tests have "come back positive and reassuring." Henderson, in a statement posted to social media on Friday, said "the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable." "I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions," Henderson said in his post. "I am committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health. My health and long-term well-being remain my foremost priorities." Neither Henderson nor the Patriots have specified any further details about his medical situation. "He is well loved and respected on our football team," coach Mike Vrabel said after Friday's practice. "I'm trying to make sure that TreVeyon's cared for, the recovery plan is intact, he's comfortable with it, and that his wife Kenzie is cared for and understands what was going on through the process. "To support him the best way I know how is just to care for him, listen to him, and do whatever we can [for him] to get [healthy, get back, help this football team and do what he loves." Henderson, 24, missed Sunday's victory against the Miami Dolphins . After the Patriots' loss to the Bears on Oct. 22, Henderson participated in two practices before landing on the injury report with an illness designation on Oct. 29. He hasn't practiced since. "My wife and I are deeply grateful for family and loved ones, the New England Patriots organization, my agent, my medical team, teammates, and everyone who has offered prayers, encouragement and support," Henderson said. In six games this season, Henderson has totaled 203 rushing yards on 52 carries (3.9 avg.) with one touchdown, while adding five receptions for 45 yards. A 2025 second-round draft pick out of Ohio State, he burst onto the scene as a rookie, playing in every regular-season game and amassing 911 rushing yards on 180 carries -- 5.1 yards per carry -- with nine touchdowns. He also had 35 receptions for 221 yards and a touchdown. Vrabel also said wide receiver A.J. Brown , who didn't practice all week due to his knee injury, won't play Sunday against the Green Bay Packers . Brown also missed the team's win over the Dolphins last week.

stories.title: Bucs at Bears Q&A: Bears look to continue their dominance
stories.summary: The Bears and Bucs square off at Soldier Field on Sunday night. We spoke with Ira Kaufman of JoeBucsFan to get you insight into what Tampa will bring to the table.
stories.detailText: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers warms up prior to the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears haven’t trailed in a game since October 11th. They haven’t trailed with Caleb Williams since September 20th. They look to continue their domination against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football. The Bucs have won 3 of their last 4 and look to continue their winning ways against the Bears. To get you set for this game, we chatted with Ira Kaufman, a long-time Bucs reporter (and Hall of Fame voter), currently with JoeBucsFan, for insight on the Bears. Here’s that Q&A. 1. Do the Tampa fans have any confidence in Todd Bowles? I know the Bucs are just a half game out of first, but this is a team that is 5-12 over their last 17 games. Todd Bowles remains an unpopular figure for much of Buc Nation. Fans aren’t happy with his clock management or his placid demeanor on the sidelines, suggesting he is being out-coached on a regular basis. A recent poll on the joebucsfan.com website revealed that more than 70 percent of voters have little or no confidence in Bowles, who is 38-38 since replacing Bruce Arians in 2022. 2. I feel like if Tampa is going to be competitive this week, Baker Mayfield is going to have to be effective in the passing game. Is he at a point where he can do that with the injured thumb? He’s only thrown 14 passes the last two weeks. Mayfield said this week that his injured right thumb has progressed to the point he no longer needs to wear a glove for support. Since he returned, Mayfield has thrown sparingly as Tampa Bay relied on a powerful ground game to defeat Carolina and Atlanta, climbing back into the race for the NFC South title. 3. The Bucs have certainly been powered by their running game, and the Bears have been susceptible to giving up some yards on the ground this season. Enter Jeffery Simmons. How do you think the Bucs can run the football against the Bears’ new front with Big Jeff? We just saw Simmons make an immediate impact as the Bears shut down Seattle on the road Monday night. However, the Seahawks don’t have an elite running back like Bucky Irving, who is averaging 5.0 yards per carry. Add in Kenneth Gainwell and a physical offensive line, and it’s fair to say Chicago’s rush defense faces a major challenge. It’s the best way for the Bucs to keep Caleb Williams and company watching from the sidelines. 4. Who is a lesser-known player on the Bucs offense and one on the Bucs defense that you think could have an impact in this game that fans may not know a lot about? The Bucs are looking for a No. 1 target to emerge in the wake of Mike Evans’ departure to the 49ers. Rookie Ted Hurst has shown flashes as a big-bodied WR who can get downfield. He earned Mayfield’s trust during an impressive training camp, and he could be a factor Sunday night. On defense, second-year pro David Walker is developing into a dynamic pass rusher who could pressure Williams into mistakes. 5. The Bucs defense has been playing excellent football. What is the key to this unit that sets them apart? Bowles overhauled his defense in the offseason, adding veterans like Al-Quadin Muhammad, A’Shawn Robinson, Alex Anzalone, and rookie Josiah Trotter. It took a few weeks, but this revamped unit has grown comfortable with the aggressive, blitzing schemes Bowles is known for. Cornerbacks Jacob Parrish (league-leading 13 pass breakups) and Zyon McCollum have been exceptional.

stories.title: Brandon Aubrey has confidence in everything around him
stories.summary: Brandon Aubrey has confidence in his support system
stories.detailText: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images When it comes to kickers, the Dallas Cowboys are quite fortunate. This season has been a little bit rough in some moments, but ultimately the Cowboys still employ one of the best around in Brandon Aubrey. It is unbelievable to consider that 2026 is already year number four for Aubrey. Aubrey has been around the Cowboys so long that he has the proper marks to prove it. He was with the team when they last made the playoffs, a group that is starting to dwindle, and he even has a second contract with the club which means he has really walked through fire. Aubrey is someone who takes care of himself and recently he has begun to do so by partnering with Invisalign and their “SHIFT Happens” mindset, something that he is considering both on and off the field. This week I had a chance to talk to him thanks to Invisalign, and you can watch our entire conversation below. It was a treat to talk to Aubrey about some of the specific natures of kicking in today’s NFL. We spent a good bit of time talking about his preparation and also how he has handled the new kickoff in terms of trying to pin opponents in specific circumstances. One thing I was curious about was whether or not he believes his own success has played a part in how the Cowboys operate things on offense. My point was that some believe that Aubrey’s range from downtown leads to Brian Schottenheimer becoming dependent on that when the Cowboys do get into field goal range. Obviously right now there is a bit of a feeling from fans that Schottenheimer is operating conservatively so take all of this with a grain of salt, but I found Brandon’s answer on that specific question to be very interesting. Has Brandon Aubrey’s success from deep changed how the Cowboys approach getting into or handling field goal range? I was curious so I asked Brandon. pic.twitter.com/cTudDo2Hc8 — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) November 6, 2026 “I don’t think when you’re looking at, I don’t I can’t speak for play callers or coaching staff’s mindsets, but for me if I were in that position I think I would have a couple of different ideas based on where I am on the field. And field goal range wherever that is for your kicker is one mindset, one play style especially if it’s like a one score game.” “I’ll say we’ve been in a lot of high scoring games so you can’t necessarily think that way I guess. You’d always wanna score a touchdown if you can. But yeah, I think when you’re in field goal range, you tend to not want to turn the ball over just because at that point you’re very obviously giving up points. So yeah I can see possibly being a little more conservative when you’re in field goal range. I don’t know what our play calling mindset is. I’m not involved in any of those decisions. I just try to be ready to kick it when when my name’s called.” This was a fair answer from Aubrey. He was specific in saying that he was only speaking for himself in a hypothetical world where he made those types of decisions, and he noted that you want to protect your opportunity to score points. That is fair and rational. But the feel and reality of our current moment is hard to ignore. Consider that the Cowboys entered Week 9 with the lowest amount of attempted fourth down conversions (on 4th and 5 or shorter) when already inside of field goal range. On one hand it suggests that the Cowboys try to secure points when it feels like they have them. On the other it opens the door of conversation as to whether or not they are perhaps too reliant upon that, which is why I asked Aubrey the question in the first place. What do you think? stories.title: Is Cam Skattebo playing this week? Latest injury update on Giants RB
stories.summary: Is Cam Skattebo playing for the Giants in Week 9? Here's the latest on the star RB's status as he battles a hamstring injury.
stories.detailText: The New York Giants are dealing with an injury to their clear-cut top running back coming off their bye week. Cam Skattebo is dealing with a hamstring injury that he suffered on the final carry of his Week 7 game against the Houston Texans. He pulled up lame at the end of a 42-yard run in overtime and ceded the field for the final snap, which resulted in a game-winning, 30-yard Devin Singletary touchdown run. Skattebo didn't seem concerned about his injury after the game, so many believed the second-year running back would be good to go for the team's Week 9 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Instead, Skattebo has continued to be absent from practice, which has thrown his status into flux. Here's what to know about Skattebo's injury and when he might return to the field for the division-leading Giants . Is Cam Skattebo playing Week 9? The Giants are listing Skattebo as "doubtful" to play in the team's Week 9 game against the Eagles. The second-year running back was unable to practice leading up to the game, being listed as a non-participant at all three of New York's sessions. John Harbaugh didn't rule Skattebo out during his media availability following Friday's practice, per ESPN's Jordan Raanan . However, the new designation would suggest Skattebo is unlikely to play, a fact that could be strengthened if the Giants elevate a running back from their practice squad on Saturday. If Skattebo doesn't play in Week 9, his next chance to suit up will be the Giants' "Thursday Night Football" game against the Washington Commanders in Week 10. When will Cam Skattebo return? The Giants have not yet provided a definitive timeline for Skattebo's return to the field. Harbaugh didn't seem overly concerned about Skattebo's absence being of the long-term variety. He referred to the running back as "day-to-day" entering the practice week while saying the team would take a wait-and-see approach with the 24-year-old. During a Wednesday, Nov. 4 press conference, Harbaugh also alluded to the tricky nature of predicting recovery for soft-tissue injuries, like hamstring problems. "Skatt's got a hamstring, so you know how that goes," Harbaugh said , referring to Skattebo by his nickname. "We'll see." Who is Cam Skattebo's backup? Devin Singletary is currently entrenched as the clear-cut backup to Skattebo. The 29-year-old veteran is in his third season with the Giants but has played sparingly to date, racking up 80 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries. Singletary produced exactly 437 rushing yards in each of his first two seasons with the Giants while serving largely as a backup or third-string option. The 2019 third-round pick posted three seasons with at least 1,000 scrimmage yards from 2021-23 and would get a lion's share of New York's backfield workload if Skattebo can't play. Giants RB depth chart The Giants presently have three running backs on their 53-man roster, as normal backup Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on IR with a hamstring injury while veteran Najee Harris was released earlier in the season. Below is a look at the pecking order within the unit. Cam Skattebo Devin Singletary Greg Desrosiers Desrosiers is an undrafted rookie who played collegiately at Louisville, UMass and Memphis before joining the NFL ranks. He originally signed with the Los Angeles Chargers but was released following final cuts and joined their practice squad. The Giants inked Desrosier to their 53-man roster to poach him from the Chargers, so he may get a first crack at backing up Singletary with Skattebo out. The Giants also have Grant Finley , Eric Gray and Phil Mafah on the practice squad, so any could be called up to provide additional depth. Gray has almost exclusively been with the Giants since being selected in the fifth round of the 2023 NFL Draft, save for a month-long stint with the Cleveland Browns' practice squad earlier this season. His familiarity with the Giants and special teams skills could prove to be a tiebreaker when New York assesses its potential call-ups. stories.title: Friday Cheese Curds: Packers are plagued by missed opportunities
stories.summary: Green Bay's receivers are leaving an alarming number of plays on the field.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Green Bay Packers don’t appear to have a problem finding open receivers. Receivers catching the ball, however, is unfortunately a problem. We’ve seen the stat six hundred times already, but here it is once more for posterity: Through eight games, Green Bay has recorded 23 dropped passes, eight more than any other NFL team. And don’t look now, but that’s already more than the Packers had all of last season. As Jordan Love continues to put together an outstanding year, drops are becoming impossible to ignore. The biggest surprise in all of this is Matthew Golden, who was drafted in part specifically because he is incredibly sure-handed. In his first training camp, months removed from a season where Packers receivers again struggled to make tough catches, Golden reportedly caught everything. In 2026, he has nine drops. But this isn’t exclusively a Golden problem. The issue has spread throughout a receiving group that has otherwise demonstrated plenty of big-play potential. Ok, let’s stop piling on. There’s reason for optimism. Christian Watson and Golden have shown the ability to make tough catches generate explosive plays. Tucker Kraft has, too — and I’d expect him to start accumulating impressive plays as he continues to regain confidence following a return from a knee injury. The talent is there, we’ve seen the proof before, and Love clearly has confidence in his receivers. That’s what makes the problem so frustrating. Green Bay doesn’t necessarily need to find another receiver before the November 10 trade deadline. It needs the very talented receivers already on the roster to catch the dang ball. Until then, they’ll continue to be a streaky offense with a quarterback leading the league in passing yards. If the pass catchers can turn it around, though, the passing attack could graduate to the “most dangerous in the league” conversation. That’ll also be necessary for this team to survive the NFC North and do damage in the playoffs. I dunno, can we go back to making them catch bricks or something? Packers lead NFL in drops by a huge margin The Green Bay Packers currently hold a wide and possibly insurmountable lead for dropped passes as the midway point of the 2026 season approaches. Packers must be buyers at trade deadline The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday. The Packers haven’t been buyers in a long time but there is a green-and-golden opportunity to make a move in the wide-open NFC. Packers give Micah Parsons boost in return from ACL injury The defense just needed to hold the line until Parsons could return from injury, but what they’ve accomplished is far more impressive. Battle of the Bay: Raider Nation versus Niner Gang
teamStories.summary: Klint Kubiak returns to battle in Levi’s Stadium. A place he knows well, having won both at home and on the road.
teamStories.detailText: The San Francisco 49ers host the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday at Levi’s Stadium. The focus on this used to be bragging rights for Raider Nation vs. Niner Gang as both teams were Bay Area rivals until the Raiders moved to Las Vegas. In the grand scheme of things, it’s just another game on the schedule for both teams. However, it’s a bigger game for the Raiders than the 49ers, as the Raiders need a statement win against a top team. Bringing a (4-4) record back to the Bay is cool and all, but for a fringe team on the outside looking in, it’s a measuring stick. Head coach Klint Kubiak is no stranger to playing and defeating the 49ers, but he is also a member of the Kyle Shanahan coaching tree. Black O vs Red D The strength of the Raiders is in their offense, specifically their passing game. However, since making the switch to Mike Washington Jr. as running back 1, with former first-round pick Ashton Jeanty as a complementary back, the rushing attack has picked up steam and a season-high 38 points were scored. Against the 49ers, the Raiders face one of the toughest defenses they have seen all season. As if that weren’t enough, it’s a defense starting to get its fangs back. While the 49ers defense may not be as great as it once was, it’s still plenty good enough to bully the Raiders offense. Fred Warner is still amongst the top dogs at linebacker, Dre Greenlaw is hitting anything not in the same colored jersey before and after the whistle. Nick Bosa is finally feeling healthy and the reacquisition of DeForest Buckner is ready to challenge the Raiders’ pass protection and newfound success on the ground. Where the game will be won Shanahan has turned the 49ers into perennial playoff contenders behind both an ever-evolving offense and a ferocious defense. Just when teams think they have the offense pegged, they find a different way to exploit the matchups and personnel and break them down. Kubiak was Shanahan’s former passing game coordinator. Now, his little brother, Klay Kubiak, is the offensive coordinator for the 49ers. Klay benefits from experimenting against a Top-5 NFL defense in practice every day. Sunday, he will be calling plays against one of the most underperforming defenses in the league. Furthermore, the 49ers offense relies on scheming players open, utilizing rhythm, timing and deception. All things that Rob Leonard and the Raiders’ defense have struggled with over the last five weeks. Leonard’s seat has to be getting hotter and hotter each week another team drops 30+ on his defense. Yes, this was the murderers’ row stretch of opponents. There are no excuses for losing; you are what your record says you are, and the Raiders are a .500 team because the offense is good and the defense isn’t. Sure, Leonard has the unenviable task of trying to corral a supremely efficient offensive machine. But they don’t call it “The Battle of the Bay” for no reason. Raider Nation v. Bang Bang Let’s be honest, life has been hard for Raider Nation. All the losing and watching members of the Nation convert to the Bang Bang Niner Gang. Why? Because the 49ers have had their stuff together and just kept winning. Growing up in the Bay Area, this rivalry means a little something extra. It is a little bit more personal than a divisional matchup because most Bay Area families and friends are split down the middle. Knocking those smug looks off the faces of the Niners Faithful just really warms the hearts of members of Raider Nation. The bragging rights silence endless ridicule and incessant reckless rambling, but not only that; it allows the Nation to hold their heads high no matter how the season ends, provided the 49ers don’t win it all.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders’ won 38-33 at the New York Jets on Sunday . Let’s review how their wide receivers fared: Tre Tucker Tucker played a team high 54 percent of the snaps, a team high. Still, it was a season low for him. He had no receptions on one target. This came after a two-game stretch in which he had 10 catches for 200 yards and three scores. Jalen Nailor: The starter played 46 percent of the snaps, a week after he played 75 percent of the snaps. He did, however, have his best game as he caught four passes on four targets for 38 yards and a score. Maybe less is more for Nailor, who had eight catches for 75 yards on 20 targets going into Sunday’s game. Jack Bech: The 2025 second-round draft pick returned from a four-game stint on the injured reserve. He played 40 percent of the snaps. Yet, he wasn’t targeted. Dareke Young: He played five offensive snap. He didn’t have any targets. Cody White: White played two snaps with no targets. He was released Wednesday and tight end Carter Runyon was activated. Then, Thursday, White was re-signed and Runyon was released. Conclusion: Nailor was the only Las Vegas wide receiver with a reception and they were targeted just five times. However, tight end Brock Bowers had six catches for 87 yards while lined up as a receiver, according to Next Gen Stats, the most for an NFL tight end in 10 seasons. We will see if that trend continues. But the Raiders need to get the ball to Tucker and Bech needs to show he deserves to be on the field. With White gone, maybe Dont’e Thornton or Malik Benson will be active Sunday.
